description:
Crew Apollo is a three-member team from Mymensingh, Bangladesh, passionate about space, data, AI/ML and problem-solving. 
MD. Morsadul Islam (Team lead, developer), 
Alif Mahmud (lead developer, 3D design) and 
Snigdha Rani Das (ML engineer, research) 
combine software, AI/ML, data analysis, 3D design and communication. We built AstroDocX on a tested, explainable engine and open NASA data, and share our code under the MIT license.
summary:
Question from an enthusiastic Mind, How do astronauts survive in space? Then we started research and found a lot about astronaut's health issues and we decided to find the solution of health issues from that thought we built AstroDocX using Nasa's public health datasets.
On a long mission a doctor can be many minutes away, so astronauts must spot slow changes in their own health and decide what to do. AstroDocX is an offline health co-pilot for this challenge: it learns each person's own normal across 11 health and cabin measures, flags drift early, and explains every alert with what changed, by how much, and which NASA research backs it. Each alert comes with a clear action card, and a ground view shows flight surgeons only what has reached Earth, and how old it
is. Real NASA Inspiration4 blood data is shown beside our test mission. It is a research prototype, not a medical device, but it turns a number on a screen into a decision a crew can trust.
details:
AstroDocX

.

(Astronaut + Doctor + X) is an offline-first health co-pilot for astronauts on long-duration missions.

Beyond the Moon, a message to Earth takes minutes each way, so the crew has to notice health changes in themselves and decide what to do. AstroDocX learns each astronaut's personal baseline, spots drift early, and turns every alert into a clear action: Detect, Explain, Act, Log, Sync later. It is organised around NASA's five spaceflight hazards (RIDGE): Radiation, Isolation, Distance from Earth, Gravity and Hostile closed Environments.

.

.

HOW IT WORKS

- Crew Console (installable offline PWA):

A Status Board with readiness and a 3D Health Twin, alerts that say what changed, by how much and against whose baseline, with NASA evidence and checkable steps, trends, a daily check-in, a mission simulator, and a delay-tolerant Ground Sync with a 12-minute delay and link windows. A Ground View lets a flight surgeon on Earth see the crew.

.

.

- VITA The AI crew doctor:

A 3D doctor with lip sync who examines the whole crew, puts people in triage order, checks EVA clearance and writes an SBAR handoff for the ground. The exam is deterministic rules. An optional live layer (Claude) may only re-word it, and the server rejects any reply with names or numbers the exam does not contain.

.

.

- NOVA, the Homepage Guide:

Answers questions with NASA citations and works without a network. Also has voice navigation system and can guide a 2 minutes full tour.

.

.

- 3D Cabin:

An ISS-style module driven by live data, with a helmet visor HUD, six crew with live name tags, wall screens that run the real console, and an EVA outside.

.

.

.

- Sensors:

.

Webcam face scan:

X-Ray Mirror:

(our own rPPG pipeline plus MediaPipe, all on the device) for heart rate, breathing and HRV

.

.

Haylou Solar 5 smartwatch:

over Web Bluetooth.

.

.

Wi-Fi sensing:

.

.

Ultrasound screens:

are simulated today and show where real hardware plugs in.

.

.

- On-device ML (Isolation Forest, Holt-Winters forecast, readiness score, watch-vs-webcam agreement) runs in the browser in shadow mode. It never feeds the alert engine.

.

.

- Voice navigation: Synthesised sound and a 2-minute guided tour (https://astrodocx.vercel.app/?tour=full).

.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT:

Crews get early warning and plain next steps without waiting for Earth. Everything works offline, and data syncs when a link window opens. Because every alert is traceable to NASA-STD-3001 limits, NASA studies and the person's own baseline, crews and flight surgeons can trust and check it. The same approach could also help remote clinics and polar stations.

.

.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

React 19, TypeScript, Vite PWA, IndexedDB (Dexie), Zustand, Recharts, three.js, WebGL, Web Audio API, Web Bluetooth, MediaPipe Tasks Vision, GSAP, Vitest, Python serverless functions, optional Supabase and Claude for wording. NASA data: Human Research Program (five hazards), NASA-STD-3001, OSDR (Inspiration4 lab panel), NTRS, NASA Image and Video Library, Visible Earth, Twins Study.

.

.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

The astronaut can walk through the cabin and work the real console on its wall screens. Hardware is replaceable: simulated sensors are written so real devices (a Wi-Fi CSI board, an ultrasound probe) can be plugged in later. Voice, sound and a guided tour make it easy to explore in minutes.

.

.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Safety: the watch, webcam and ML never raise medical alerts, and AI never invents numbers. Privacy: video never leaves the device and the watch data stays local. Honesty: the demo mission and the Wi-Fi and ultrasound readings are synthetic, and only the CO2 and dose limits are cited NASA limits. AstroDocX is a prototype, not a medical device.

Live app: https://astrodocx.vercel.app
Source code: https://github.com/A-42-018/AstroDocX
